key_insight: Deep learning often defies classical statistical intuition, and its performance can be understood through neural scaling laws and problem-specific inductive biases from a physics-informed perspective.
engineering_relevance: For scientific machine learning, model choice, constraints, and prior structure can strongly affect accuracy and data efficiency when applying AI to physical systems.
method: Review deep learning behavior through a physics-informed lens
Summarize neural scaling laws and their implications
Discuss how inductive biases and constraints shape learning in physics applications
evidence_signal: The paper is a conceptual review, so its support comes from synthesizing observed deep learning behavior rather than reporting a single new benchmark or dataset.
watch_item: Scaling-law insights may not transfer directly across tasks unless the model architecture, constraints, and data regime are carefully matched to the target physics problem.
